purpose: Diagnose the missing absolute field after P0675-P0677 by decomposing the already spent training-only compact-halo comparator relative to the P0674 baryonic scalar field on one grid, without fitting a new gravity law or scoring image roots.

compact_halo_selection.interpretation: the NIE plus external shear is a successful spent comparator field, not a dark-matter truth map

decomposition.monopole: within-bin mean radial deflection times the local radial unit vector
decomposition.angular_residual: compact-halo deflection minus the reconstructed monopole
decomposition.convergence: kappa=0.5(d alpha_x/dx+d alpha_y/dy) on the reference-source reduced field
decomposition.criticality: sign-changing cells of det[I-d alpha/d theta] for scalar, scalar+halo, and scalar+halo+shear

selection_rule: P0678 is diagnostic and does not advance a formula. It must preserve every integrity gate and report the required field even if baryonic correlations are weak. A later candidate may use only relationships computed from baryons; target-derived compact-halo quantities cannot appear as its inputs.
claim_boundary: RX J2129 and its compact-halo fit are fully spent development data; P0678 cannot validate a new law.
The compact halo is a low-parameter successful comparator, not a unique reconstruction of dark matter or the true lens potential.
Combining the P0674 scalar map with a halo fitted beside a different baryonic radial profile is a missing-field diagnostic, not a refitted lens model.
Finite-difference convergence and criticality on a 33-cell grid are approximate and cannot replace raw topology or resolution convergence.
P0633 galaxy kinematics and P0640 additional-cluster lens outcomes remain sealed.
